title: Ethel Smyth's birth chart
metaDescription: Ethel Smyth's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 2.0° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Six of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Taurus — the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Uranus and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 2.0° of Taurus is the Sun's exact seat — first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Venus in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 21.9° Taurus, Venus was at 15.4° Taurus, Mars was at 1.3° Sagittarius. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that grows by reliability; effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Jupiter and Saturn: 0.0° from an exact sextile. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, Mercury sextile Saturn at 0.4°, and Mercury conjunction Jupiter at 0.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. Venus in Taurus at 15.4° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Cancer at 22.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 6 in earth, 2 in water, 1 in fire by element, 6 fixed, 2 mutable, 1 cardinal by modality. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mars was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Leo into Virgo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.3° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
